description: Japan's Ambassador for Mekong Cooperation, Teiji Hayashi, completed a May 31–June 2 mission to Cambodia and Thailand aimed at easing bilateral tensions. He held consultations with Cambodian officials on June 1 and Thai officials on June 2, urging steady implementation of the ceasefire agreement, maximum restraint and peaceful dialogue toward normalizing relations. Japan said Hayashi and senior officials of both countries also agreed to strengthen coordination on de-escalation.

description: On June 2, Royal Thai Army spokesperson Maj. Gen. Winthai Suvaree responded to Cambodia's protest over Buddha statues, Thai flags, other border structures and barbed wire. He said the statues and flags were in areas under Thai sovereignty and control and were intended to support troop and civilian morale; he said the barbed wire at Chong Bok was a security measure to protect personnel and reduce the risk of confrontation. These were Thailand's claims about disputed border areas, not an independent determination of sovereignty.

description: On June 2, Royal Thai Navy spokesman Rear Adm. Paraj Ratanajaipan said the Chanthaburi and Trat Border Defence Command would facilitate an Immigration Bureau operation that afternoon to return 47 Cambodian nationals through the Ban Laem permanent checkpoint in Chanthaburi. He said the group had completed Thailand's judicial process and described the transfer as a legal repatriation, not a reopening or relaxation of border controls.

description: On June 2, Cambodia said it had delivered formal notice to Thailand and the UN Secretary-General to institute compulsory conciliation under Annex V of UNCLOS over maritime delimitation in the Gulf of Thailand. The step followed Thailand's termination of the 2001 maritime memorandum. Cambodian reporting also said Phnom Penh had selected two conciliators, Peter Taksøe-Jensen and Jean-Marc Thouvenin, while the UNCLOS procedure gave Thailand 21 days after receipt of the notification to appoint two conciliators of its own.

description: On June 2, Thai and Cambodian troops faced off in the Mom Bei/Chong Bok area after Thai troops began bunker and barbed-wire work. Thailand's Second Army Region said about 20 Cambodian soldiers objected and obstructed the work from 08:50; Cambodian reporting said Cambodian troops intervened because they considered the wire to be on Cambodian territory. Thai reporting said the wire work finished at 10:30 and the Cambodian troops withdrew at 11:08 without an armed clash. An ASEAN Observer Team was separately visiting An Ses in Preah Vihear province that day; available evidence does not place it at the Chong Bok standoff.

description: On June 5, Thai PBS World reported that Thailand's Second Army Region released images it said showed Cambodian troops planting anti-tank improvised explosive devices near Hill 745, close to the Chong Bok border pass in Nam Yuen district, Ubon Ratchathani. The Army said it released the images to challenge a Cambodian military denial. Cambodia's denial said it could not confirm the origin of the claimed IEDs or identify the troops accused of planting them. Based on uniforms and insignia visible in the images, the Thai Army claimed the troops were from Cambodia's 21st infantry corps. The captured report establishes the Thai military's release and competing claims; it does not independently verify who planted the devices or the unit identification. It gives no exact event time.

description: On June 5, Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said Thailand would appoint two conciliators and participate in the compulsory UNCLOS conciliation initiated by Cambodia. He continued to argue that bilateral talks should have been tried first. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul separately said Thailand would put other bilateral talks, including land-border discussions, on hold and keep border gates closed. This milestone records Thailand's June 5 public decision to participate in the process.

description: On June 5, Cambodia’s Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts condemned what it described as the destruction by Thai military forces of the wooden staircase leading to K’nar Temple. The ministry said the staircase had 1,181 steps, extended 325 metres, and was built by Cambodian authorities in 2017 for heritage conservation and access. It characterized the damage as harm to cultural heritage and linked the issue to Cambodia’s sovereignty claims. These are Cambodian government allegations and legal positions; the cited statement does not independently establish who destroyed the staircase or an exact incident time.
descriptionKh: នៅថ្ងៃទី 5 ខែមិថុនា ក្រសួងវប្បធម៌ និងវិចិត្រសិល្បៈកម្ពុជា បានថ្កោលទោសអ្វីដែលខ្លួនពិពណ៌នាថា ជាការបំផ្លាញជណ្ដើរឈើឡើងប្រាសាទ K’nar ដោយកងកម្លាំងយោធាថៃ។ ក្រសួងបាននិយាយថា ជណ្ដើរនេះមាន 1,181 កាំ ប្រវែង 325 ម៉ែត្រ និងត្រូវបានអាជ្ញាធរកម្ពុជាសាងសង់នៅឆ្នាំ 2017 សម្រាប់ការអភិរក្សបេតិកភណ្ឌ និងការចូលដល់តំបន់។ ក្រសួងបានពិពណ៌នាការខូចខាតនេះថាជាការប៉ះពាល់ដល់បេតិកភណ្ឌវប្បធម៌ និងភ្ជាប់បញ្ហានេះទៅនឹងការអះអាងអធិបតេយ្យភាពរបស់កម្ពុជា។ ទាំងនេះជាការចោទប្រកាន់ និងជំហរផ្លូវច្បាប់របស់រដ្ឋាភិបាលកម្ពុជា ហើយសេចក្តីថ្លែងការណ៍ដែលបានយោងមិនបានបញ្ជាក់ដោយឯករាជ្យថា អ្នកណាបានបំផ្លាញជណ្ដើរ ឬម៉ោងកើតហេតុជាក់លាក់ទេ។
descriptionTh: เมื่อวันที่ 5 มิถุนายน กระทรวงวัฒนธรรมและวิจิตรศิลป์กัมพูชาประณามสิ่งที่กระทรวงอธิบายว่าเป็นการทำลายบันไดไม้ขึ้นปราสาท K’nar โดยกำลังทหารไทย กระทรวงระบุว่าบันไดมี 1,181 ขั้น ยาว 325 เมตร และสร้างโดยทางการกัมพูชาในปี 2017 เพื่อการอนุรักษ์มรดกและการเข้าถึงพื้นที่ กระทรวงระบุว่าความเสียหายดังกล่าวเป็นความเสียหายต่อมรดกวัฒนธรรมและเชื่อมโยงประเด็นนี้กับข้ออ้างอธิปไตยของกัมพูชา ข้อความเหล่านี้เป็นข้อกล่าวหาและจุดยืนทางกฎหมายของรัฐบาลกัมพูชา แถลงการณ์ที่อ้างถึงไม่ได้ยืนยันโดยอิสระว่าใครเป็นผู้ทำลายบันไดหรือเวลาเกิดเหตุที่แน่นอน

description: On June 9, Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul held an informal discussion before the opening of the ASEAN Future Forum in Vietnam; details of the discussion were not released. description: On June 16, Thailand announced the appointment of Judge Rüdiger Wolfrum of Germany and Judge Albert J. Hoffmann of South Africa as its two conciliators in the compulsory conciliation process initiated by Cambodia under UNCLOS. Both are former presidents of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea. Reporting on June 17–18 said Cambodia had also named Peter Taksøe-Jensen and Jean-Marc Thouvenin; The Star noted that Cambodia's selections were initially reported from unofficial sources. Under the UNCLOS mechanism, once all four conciliators are nominated, the parties have one month to agree on a fifth member to chair the commission.

Hoffmann នៃអាហ្វ្រិកខាងត្បូង ជាអ្នកសម្រុះសម្រួលពីររូបរបស់ខ្លួនក្នុងដំណើរការសម្រុះសម្រួលជាកាតព្វកិច្ចដែលកម្ពុជាបានផ្តួចផ្តើមក្រោម UNCLOS។ អ្នកទាំងពីរជាអតីតប្រធានតុលាការអន្តរជាតិស្តីពីច្បាប់សមុទ្រ។ សេចក្តីរាយការណ៍នៅថ្ងៃទី 17–18 ខែមិថុនាបាននិយាយថា កម្ពុជាក៏បានជ្រើសរើស Peter Taksøe-Jensen និង Jean-Marc Thouvenin ផងដែរ ខណៈ The Star បានកត់សម្គាល់ថា ការជ្រើសរើសរបស់កម្ពុជាដំបូងត្រូវបានរាយការណ៍តាមប្រភពមិនផ្លូវការ។ តាមយន្តការ UNCLOS បន្ទាប់ពីអ្នកសម្រុះសម្រួលទាំងបួនត្រូវបានតែងតាំង ភាគីទាំងពីរមានរយៈពេលមួយខែដើម្បីព្រមព្រៀងលើសមាជិកទីប្រាំដែលនឹងធ្វើជាប្រធានគណៈកម្មការ។

Hoffmann แห่งแอฟริกาใต้ เป็นผู้ประนีประนอม 2 คนของไทยในกระบวนการประนอมข้อพิพาทภาคบังคับที่กัมพูชาเริ่มภายใต้ UNCLOS ทั้งสองเป็นอดีตประธานศาลกฎหมายทะเลระหว่างประเทศ รายงานวันที่ 17–18 มิถุนายนระบุว่ากัมพูชาได้เลือก Peter Taksøe-Jensen และ Jean-Marc Thouvenin เช่นกัน โดย The Star ระบุว่ารายชื่อฝ่ายกัมพูชาในช่วงแรกมาจากแหล่งข่าวที่ไม่เป็นทางการ ตามกลไก UNCLOS เมื่อมีการเสนอชื่อผู้ประนีประนอมครบทั้ง 4 คนแล้ว ทั้งสองฝ่ายมีเวลา1 เดือนเพื่อตกลงเลือกสมาชิกคนที่ 5 เป็นประธานคณะกรรมการ

description: On June 18 at around 04:00, the Royal Thai Navy said the Chanthaburi Marine Task Force found and detained 50 people walking with luggage near Ban Pa Khoi in Pong Nam Ron district, Chanthaburi. The Navy said the group included 27 men, 17 women and six children, with 10 men acting as paid porters and guides. Detainees told officials they intended to return to Cambodia through a natural border route after paying smugglers. Authorities transferred the group to immigration and police for legal proceedings.
descriptionKh: នៅថ្ងៃទី 18 ខែមិថុនា ប្រហែលម៉ោង 04:00 កងទ័ពជើងទឹកថៃបាននិយាយថា កងកម្លាំងនាវិកយោធាចន្ទបុរីបានរកឃើញ និងឃាត់ខ្លួនមនុស្ស 50 នាក់ដែលកំពុងដើរជាមួយអីវ៉ាន់នៅក្បែរភូមិ Ban Pa Khoi ស្រុក Pong Nam Ron ខេត្តចន្ទបុរី។ កងទ័ពជើងទឹកបាននិយាយថា ក្រុមនេះមានបុរស 27 នាក់ ស្ត្រី 17 នាក់ និងកុមារ 6 នាក់ ហើយបុរស 10 នាក់ធ្វើជាអ្នកស៊ីឈ្នួលសែងអីវ៉ាន់ និងនាំផ្លូវ។ អ្នកត្រូវឃាត់ខ្លួនបានប្រាប់អាជ្ញាធរថា ពួកគេចង់ត្រឡប់ទៅកម្ពុជាតាមច្រកធម្មជាតិ បន្ទាប់ពីបង់ប្រាក់ឱ្យបណ្តាញលួចនាំមនុស្សឆ្លងដែន។ អាជ្ញាធរបានបញ្ជូនក្រុមនេះទៅឱ្យអន្តោប្រវេសន៍ និងប៉ូលិសដើម្បីចាត់ការតាមច្បាប់។
descriptionTh: เมื่อวันที่ 18 มิถุนายน เวลาประมาณ 04:00 น. กองทัพเรือไทยระบุว่า หน่วยเฉพาะกิจนาวิกโยธินจันทบุรีพบและควบคุมตัวบุคคล 50 คนที่เดินพร้อมสัมภาระใกล้บ้านป่าข่อย อำเภอโป่งน้ำร้อน จังหวัดจันทบุรี กองทัพเรือระบุว่ากลุ่มดังกล่าวมีชาย 27 คน หญิง 17 คน และเด็ก 6 คน โดยมีชาย 10 คนรับจ้างแบกสัมภาระและนำทาง ผู้ถูกควบคุมตัวให้การต่อเจ้าหน้าที่ว่าต้องการกลับกัมพูชาผ่านช่องทางธรรมชาติหลังจ่ายเงินให้เครือข่ายลักลอบนำพา เจ้าหน้าที่ส่งตัวกลุ่มดังกล่าวให้ตรวจคนเข้าเมืองและตำรวจดำเนินการตามกฎหมาย

description: During the June 18 ASEAN-Russia Commemorative Summit in Kazan, Hun Manet said he held an informal discussion with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and reiterated Cambodia’s positions: peaceful resolution under international law, continued UNCLOS compulsory conciliation for maritime issues, and JBC mechanisms for the land border. The captured sources do not establish a mutual Thai-Cambodian commitment from that conversation.
descriptionKh: ក្នុងអំឡុងកិច្ចប្រជុំកំពូលអាស៊ាន-រុស្ស៊ីនៅកាហ្សាន ថ្ងៃទី 18 ខែមិថុនា ហ៊ុន ម៉ាណែត បាននិយាយថា លោកបានពិភាក្សាក្រៅផ្លូវការជាមួយនាយករដ្ឋមន្ត្រីថៃ អនុទីន ឆានវីរកុល ហើយបានបញ្ជាក់ឡើងវិញនូវជំហររបស់កម្ពុជា៖ ដោះស្រាយបញ្ហាដោយសន្តិវិធីតាមច្បាប់អន្តរជាតិ បន្តដំណើរការសម្រុះសម្រួលជាកាតព្វកិច្ចក្រោម UNCLOS សម្រាប់បញ្ហាសមុទ្រ និងប្រើយន្តការ JBC សម្រាប់ព្រំដែនគោក។ ប្រភពដែលបានរក្សាទុកមិនបញ្ជាក់ថាការសន្ទនានេះជាការប្តេជ្ញារួមរបស់ថៃនិងកម្ពុជាទេ។
descriptionTh: ระหว่างการประชุมสุดยอดอาเซียน-รัสเซียที่คาซานเมื่อวันที่ 18 มิถุนายน ฮุน มาเนตกล่าวว่าเขาได้หารืออย่างไม่เป็นทางการกับนายกรัฐมนตรีอนุทิน ชาญวีรกูล ของไทย และย้ำจุดยืนของกัมพูชา ได้แก่ การแก้ปัญหาโดยสันติตามกฎหมายระหว่างประเทศ การดำเนินกระบวนการประนอมข้อพิพาทภาคบังคับภายใต้ UNCLOS ต่อไปสำหรับปัญหาทางทะเล และการใช้กลไก JBC สำหรับปัญหาพรมแดนทางบก แหล่งข้อมูลที่บันทึกไว้ไม่ได้ยืนยันว่าการสนทนานี้เป็นคำมั่นร่วมของไทยและกัมพูชา

The report did not specify the exact date of deportation or demographic breakdown.

description: On June 19, Naewna reported Thai Army spokesperson Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree saying the Army would keep security at Prasat Khana intensive, with surveillance, stronger positions and patrol routes, and mine clearance among its priorities. Winthai said Cambodian forces had previously encroached on the high-ground area and established a military base, and said Thai forces now controlled 90% of high-ground areas of this type. Those territorial, encroachment and control characterizations are the Thai Army's account and are not independently established by the captured report. The article gives no exact event time.
descriptionKh: នៅថ្ងៃទី 19 ខែមិថុនា Naewna បានរាយការណ៍ថា អ្នកនាំពាក្យកងទ័ពថៃ ឧត្តមសេនីយ៍ត្រី Winthai Suvaree បាននិយាយថា កងទ័ពនឹងបន្តរឹតបន្តឹងសន្តិសុខនៅប្រាសាទខ្នារ ដោយផ្តោតលើការឃ្លាំមើល ការពង្រឹងទីតាំង និងផ្លូវល្បាត ព្រមទាំងការបោសសម្អាតមីន។ លោក Winthai បានអះអាងថា កងកម្លាំងកម្ពុជាធ្លាប់ចូលរំលោភតំបន់ខ្ពស់នេះ និងបង្កើតមូលដ្ឋានយោធា ហើយបាននិយាយថា បច្ចុប្បន្នកងកម្លាំងថៃគ្រប់គ្រង 90 ភាគរយនៃតំបន់ខ្ពស់ប្រភេទនេះ។ ការពិពណ៌នាអំពីដែនដី ការចូលរំលោភ និងការគ្រប់គ្រងទាំងនេះជាការរៀបរាប់របស់កងទ័ពថៃ ហើយរបាយការណ៍ដែលបានរក្សាទុកមិនបានផ្ទៀងផ្ទាត់ដោយឯករាជ្យទេ។ អត្ថបទមិនបានផ្តល់ម៉ោងព្រឹត្តិការណ៍ជាក់លាក់ទេ។
descriptionTh: เมื่อวันที่ 19 มิถุนายน แนวหน้ารายงานว่า พล.ต.วินธัย สุวารี โฆษกกองทัพบก ระบุว่ากองทัพจะยังคงคุมเข้มพื้นที่ปราสาทคนา โดยให้ความสำคัญกับการเฝ้าตรวจและเฝ้าระวัง การปรับปรุงที่มั่นและเส้นทางลาดตระเวน รวมถึงการเก็บกู้ทุ่นระเบิด วินธัยกล่าวว่ากำลังกัมพูชาเคยรุกล้ำพื้นที่สูงและตั้งฐานทหารในบริเวณดังกล่าว และกล่าวว่าปัจจุบันฝ่ายไทยควบคุมพื้นที่สูงลักษณะนี้ได้ร้อยละ 90 ข้อกล่าวเรื่องเขตแดน การรุกล้ำ และการควบคุมพื้นที่เหล่านี้เป็นคำกล่าวของกองทัพไทย และรายงานที่เก็บไว้ไม่ได้ยืนยันโดยอิสระ บทความไม่ได้ระบุเวลาเกิดเหตุที่แน่นอน

description: On June 19, Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs formally protested actions it alleged Thai forces had carried out on June 17: raising Thai flags near the Thmar Da International Border Checkpoint, burning a warehouse at the Royal O’Smach Hotel and Resort, and constructing concrete fences near Ta Krabey Temple. Cambodia described the actions as violations of its sovereignty, called for unilateral activity to stop, and reiterated that border disputes should be resolved peacefully. The territorial and responsibility claims remain Cambodia's allegations.

description: On June 19, Thailand submitted its formal Response to Cambodia's Notification of Conciliation under UNCLOS. Thailand named Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow as Agent and Ambassador Songchai Chaipatiyut as Deputy Agent, and notified Cambodia of its previously appointed conciliators, Albert J. Hoffmann and Rüdiger Wolfrum. Thailand said the process was limited to maritime-boundary delimitation and that it would participate in good faith. This is compulsory conciliation, not arbitration, and no exact submission time is supported by the captured publisher evidence.

descriptionTh: เมื่อวันที่ 19 มิถุนายน ไทยยื่นคำตอบอย่างเป็นทางการต่อหนังสือแจ้งขอประนอมข้อพิพาทของกัมพูชาภายใต้ UNCLOS โดยแต่งตั้งรัฐมนตรีต่างประเทศ Sihasak Phuangketkeow เป็นผู้แทน และเอกอัครราชทูต Songchai Chaipatiyut เป็นรองผู้แทน พร้อมแจ้งกัมพูชาถึงผู้ประนีประนอมที่ไทยแต่งตั้งไว้ก่อนแล้ว คือ Albert J. description: On June 22, Khaosod English reported that residents in Ban Nong Chan, Khok Sung district, said they had observed Cambodian troops using heavy machinery for several days to dig trenches and build defensive positions close to the Thailand-Cambodia border. description: AKP reported on June 24 that Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation issued a press release that evening protesting activities it attributed to the Thai side between June 18 and 22 near Chouk Chey village, Banteay Meanchey, along the segment between Boundary Pillars 46 and 47. Cambodia alleged that a Thai surveying team accompanied by civilians and vehicles conducted land surveys and installed boundary markers and said those actions violated the 2000 land-boundary MOU, the 2003 Terms of Reference, the October 2025 JBC minutes and December 2025 de-escalation measures. description: On June 27, Thailand's House committee on state security and border affairs inspected the permanent border-fence project in Pong Nam Ron district, Chanthaburi. Navy Captain Prachya Hanthiem told the committee that construction was 45% complete. He said a visible gap at border marker 52 was temporary because the Joint Boundary Commission process for that point was not yet complete; officials planned a hinged cover that would still allow joint inspection of the marker. The two planned phases cover about 8.3 kilometres between border markers 52 and 59.

description: On June 27, Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation issued a formal protest alleging that Thai armed forces had cleared forest and installed barbed wire near Boundary Pillar No. 26 in Ampil commune, Banteay Ampil district, Oddar Meanchey province between early June and June 23. Cambodia said the activity advanced into Cambodian territory, breached the 2000 land-boundary MOU and the December 27 de-escalation measures, and urged Thailand to cease the activity. These sovereignty, encroachment and legal-breach assertions are Cambodia's position; the captured Cambodian government report does not independently establish the boundary or a violation.

description: In a letter dated June 29, RCAF Commander-in-Chief Gen. Vong Pisen complained to Philippine Armed Forces Chief Gen. Romeo Brawner Jr., chair of the ASEAN Observer Team, about a June 26 incident near Khnar Temple. Cambodia alleged that AOT members assigned to Thailand, accompanied by Thai armed forces, entered territory Cambodia claims as sovereign without prior notification or coordination and planted trees. Vong Pisen asked the AOT chair to review the incident and ensure compliance with the team's terms of reference. This records Cambodia's complaint; it does not independently resolve the sovereignty claim.
descriptionKh: ក្នុងលិខិតចុះថ្ងៃទី 29 ខែមិថុនា នាយឧត្តមសេនីយ៍ វង្ស ពិសេន អគ្គមេបញ្ជាការកងយោធពលខេមរភូមិន្ទ បានប្តឹងទៅនាយឧត្តមសេនីយ៍ Romeo Brawner Jr. អគ្គសេនាធិការកងទ័ពហ្វីលីពីន និងជាប្រធានក្រុមអ្នកសង្កេតការណ៍អាស៊ាន (AOT) អំពីហេតុការណ៍ថ្ងៃទី 26 ខែមិថុនា នៅជិតប្រាសាទខ្នារ។ កម្ពុជាបានចោទថា សមាជិក AOT ប្រចាំប្រទេសថៃ ដែលអមដោយកងកម្លាំងប្រដាប់អាវុធថៃ បានចូលទៅក្នុងតំបន់ដែលកម្ពុជាអះអាងថាជាដែនអធិបតេយ្យភាពរបស់ខ្លួន ដោយគ្មានការជូនដំណឹង ឬសម្របសម្រួលជាមុន ហើយបានដាំដើមឈើ។ វង្ស ពិសេន បានស្នើឱ្យប្រធាន AOT ពិនិត្យហេតុការណ៍ និងធានាការអនុវត្តតាមលក្ខខណ្ឌការងាររបស់ក្រុម។ កំណត់ត្រានេះបង្ហាញពីការប្តឹងរបស់កម្ពុជា មិនមែនជាការកំណត់ដោយឯករាជ្យអំពីអធិបតេយ្យភាពទេ។
descriptionTh: ในหนังสือลงวันที่ 29 มิถุนายน พลเอก วง พิสิน ผู้บัญชาการทหารสูงสุดกัมพูชา ร้องเรียนต่อพลเอก Romeo Brawner Jr. ผู้บัญชาการทหารสูงสุดฟิลิปปินส์และประธานคณะผู้สังเกตการณ์อาเซียน (AOT) เกี่ยวกับเหตุการณ์วันที่ 26 มิถุนายนใกล้ปราสาทขนาร์ กัมพูชากล่าวหาว่าสมาชิก AOT ที่ประจำฝ่ายไทยซึ่งมีกองกำลังไทยร่วมด้วย เข้าไปในพื้นที่ที่กัมพูชาอ้างว่าเป็นอธิปไตยของตนโดยไม่มีการแจ้งหรือประสานงานล่วงหน้า และได้ปลูกต้นไม้ วง พิสิน ขอให้ประธาน AOT ตรวจสอบเหตุการณ์และกำกับให้ปฏิบัติตามข้อกำหนดของคณะผู้สังเกตการณ์ บันทึกนี้สะท้อนคำร้องเรียนของกัมพูชา ไม่ได้วินิจฉัยข้ออ้างเรื่องอธิปไตยโดยอิสระ

description: Khmer Times reported on June 30 that Cambodia's Ministry of Information protested Thailand's escort of foreign journalists, including an ABC News crew, into the O'Smach border area without prior authorisation from Cambodian authorities.
